paras: The Martin's Ferry mob of May 1903 was a gathering of several hundred people around the building in Martin's Ferry, Ohio, where two Black men suspected of attacking a young white woman were held on the night of 9 May 1903. The crowd made no attempt to take the prisoners and dispersed in about an hour, and the main suspect, William Thompson, could not be identified.

According to the Wheeling Sunday Register, a young stenographer met two Black men at Locust Grove that morning, and one struck her to the ground with the intent of 'criminal assault' before both fled at her screams.

Chief of Police Terrill found a Black man asleep by a fence near the scene and jailed him as the assailant's 'partner'. That night a Wheeling officer chased another Black man, William Thompson, into the back river and arrested him, but the woman could not positively identify him.

When residents learned that Thompson had been brought to Martin's Ferry, 'a mob of several hundred citizens gathered around the building'. Told that the officers were unsure he was the man, the crowd quieted; the Register wrote that 'all they needed was a leader' and that the prisoners 'feared for their lives.' The officers stood by to protect the prisoner, and Terrill quieted the crowd.

Terrill said he was 'almost satisfied' Thompson was not the man wanted, and a third suspect arrested at the depot on 10 May was released. No report of Thompson's release, a charge or a trial appears in the coverage.

The Wheeling Sunday Register headlined the story 'Two Negroes Attempted to Ravish Pretty White Girl' and called the accused a 'brute' and 'curs', treating the assault as established while reporting doubts about Thompson. Its subheads moved from 'Angry Mob Gathers' to 'NO DEMONSTRATION'. The Wheeling Register added a brief item on the depot arrest and, in July, a note on a revolver found in the river that was believed to be Thompson's. No coverage was found in the Black press.

reader.title: Martin's Ferry mob of May 1903
bases: A crowd of several hundred gathered around the building where two Black men accused of an assault on a white woman were held, and the paper wrote that 'all they needed was a leader', but no attempt was made to take them (A1).
No one was killed or injured by the crowd; several hundred people gathered over an alleged assault on a white woman but made no attempt to seize the prisoner and dispersed in about an hour (A1).
Only the Wheeling Sunday Register reports the crowd (A1); the Wheeling Register confirms the assault investigation and a later suspect's release but not the gathering (A2, A3).

accounts.label: Wheeling Sunday Register (local report)
accounts.gist: Two Black men attacked a young white woman; one was caught asleep near the scene and Thompson was arrested in Wheeling; several hundred people gathered but quieted when told Thompson might not be the man, and dispersed.

accounts.label: Wheeling Register Martin's Ferry column
accounts.gist: A Black man arrested at the depot as a suspect was found not to be the one wanted and released; nothing new was learned.

framing.detail: The Wheeling Sunday Register stated the assault as fact under the headline 'Two Negroes Attempted to Ravish Pretty White Girl' and called the accused 'brute' and 'curs', while reporting that the officers protected the prisoner and that there was 'NO DEMONSTRATION'.
The Wheeling Register gave the case a short paragraph headed 'Negro Arrested' in its Martin's Ferry column and later linked a found revolver to the suspect chased into the river.

versions.value: Thompson 'favored the man very much' but the woman could not positively identify him, and Chief Terrill was 'almost satisfied' he was not the man
Two months later the revolver Thompson dropped was still described as belonging to the man chased 'on suspicion of being wanted for criminal assault at Martin's Ferry'

conflicts.note: A3 does not claim Thompson was identified; it repeats only that he had been suspected. No report settles who the assailant was.

versions.value: One man jailed as the 'partner'; 'the other man could not be found'; Thompson held as a suspect
A further Black suspect arrested at the C. & P. depot on 10 May and released

conflicts.note: The depot arrest appears to be a separate, third man; A2 does not mention Thompson or the man jailed earlier.

info: Alleged assault on the morning of Saturday, 9 May 1903; Thompson arrested about 8 p.m. and the crowd gathered that night
Assault reported at Locust Grove, in sight of Martin's Ferry; crowd gathered around the building in Martin's Ferry where the prisoners were held; Thompson arrested in Wheeling, W. Va.
Two Black men held at Martin's Ferry: an unnamed man found asleep by a fence near the scene, and William Thompson, arrested in Wheeling
Accused of striking a young white woman, a Wheeling stenographer, to the ground with intent of 'criminal assault'; the man found asleep was called the 'partner' of the assailant
'Martin's Ferry people', described as 'a mob of several hundred citizens'
Thompson could not be positively identified and Terrill was 'almost satisfied' he was not the man; no report of his release, a charge or a trial of either man was found

sources.note: Main and only full report: alleged assault at Locust Grove, two Black men held, William Thompson not identified, crowd of several hundred gathered and dispersed.
quotes: a mob of several hundred citizens gathered around the building
While no attempt was made to secure the man, the demonstration showed that all they needed was a leader.
The two negroes were terribly frightened and feared for their lives.
But the young lady could not positively identify him as the man.
The Martin's Ferry officers all stood by to protect the prisoner.
